exposure: GDM subtypes with elevated fasting blood glucose (GDM-HR)
GDM subtypes without elevated fasting blood glucose (GDM-LR)
cohort: The study included 3268 pregnant women diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
finding: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) subtypes with elevated fasting blood glucose (GDM-HR) were associated with a higher risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including increased fetal birth weight, higher rates of cesarean section, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, preterm birth, macrosomia, LGA infants, and neonatal hypoglycemia, compared to GDM subtypes without elevated FBG (GDM-LR).
mod_finding: GDM-HR was associated with a higher rate of cesarean section compared to GDM-LR (aOR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.19-1.76).
